newsitem.title: USA: Corp bond deals slow before U.S Treasury refunding.
newsitem.headline: Corp bond deals slow before U.S Treasury refunding.

text.p: Corporate bond high-grade debt issuance will take a backseat for now as the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding gets underway, dealers said.
"It's been painfully quiet," said one high-grade syndicate source. "I think once the (Treasury) refunding gets digested the market will begin to see some corporate deals."

The Treasury will conduct its quarterly refunding beginning Tuesday with the sale of $17.75 billion in three-year notes, $12.0 billion in 10-year notes Wednesday and $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds Thursday.
Despite the lack of an official investment grade calendar, rumors continue to circulate of a possible Ford Motor $1.0 billion global 10-year debt offering via Merrill Lynch, syndicate sources said.
Also rumored is a five-year debt deal out of Kellogg Co, sources said.
Meanwhile, corporate debt-starved investors clamoring for more paper may be able to satisfy their appetites in another sector as a slew of high-yield debt offerings come to market.
TCI Satellite Entertainment is expected to issue its $350 million in two-part debt later this week via joint lead managers Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities and Merrill Lynch.
The deal consist of $150 million senior subordinated notes due 2006 and $200 million (proceeds) in senior subordinated discount notes due 2006.

Also, Forcenergy is expected to issue $175 million in 144A B1/B rated senior subordinated notes due 2007, callable after five years. Price talk on the issue is in the area of 220 to 230 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Dawson Production Services is also set to bring $110 million in senior notes due 2007, sources said.
Nextwave Telecommunications is also rumored to come to market with a two-part debt deal consisting of 10-year senior notes and 10-year senior discount notes, sources added.
Sun Media Corp may also issue $150 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2007 later this week, sources said.

Barret Resoures Corp is also expected to tap the market with $150 million in senior notes due 2007. The issue has a make-whole-call and is rated Ba1/BB-plus. Goldman Sachs & Co is expected to underwrite the offering, sources said.
Activity is expected to taper off as towards the end of the week. Debt players will wrap up activity early on Friday ahead of Monday's Presidents Day holiday when markets will be closed.
In the government market, the U.S. 30-year bond is off 1/32 at 97-11/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
